rule: Return-to-running ramp starts with 3 runs per week.
summary: A systematic review of endurance athletes linked training frequency below 2 sessions/week to more injury/pain (medium effect), and spreading a week's volume over 3 runs keeps each single run shorter, which matters under the single-run spike evidence. Clinical return-to-run programs typically run every other day early on, which 3 runs/week matches. The exact number is untested, but it is cheap and fits the rest of the system.

sources.note: Endurance sport systematic review: frequency < 2 sessions/week associated with higher injury/pain risk
Evidence on running frequency and injury conflicting across 36 cohorts
Injury risk tracks single-session length vs the 30-day longest; more runs per week keep each run shorter
